input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes the MFN on us, not the Vendor: we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive, before engaging another provider. It is unlimited as to product, term, and comparability, so it is an open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor — walk-away territory, well short of the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs). It also conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing needs preserving; the smallest fix reaching the preferred position is deletion of the clause.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted this clause because it obliges us to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer for Vendor's benefit — an open-ended most-favoured-nation commitment running against us, which our playbook does not accept and which contradicts Section 12.3's confirmation that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We are happy to keep any MFN pricing granted in our favour.
proposal.summary: Delete Section 7.2 MFN/match-the-offer obligation imposed on Customer
